Native-runtime preflights

        

          These probes use 8K context and short outputs to check allocation, decode speed and a
          native tool round trip. They are separate from the 32K Buro task comparison and do not
          establish repository-level code quality.
        

        

      

      

        
Review contract delivery

        

          The original Flash small-task code passed independent host checks, but one review report
          failed validation because the JSON instruction transport omitted the actual schema. Commit
          f992728 sends that contract through the generic adapter. It does not reinterpret prose as
          function calls. The original matrix remains on its frozen base. Separate contract probes
          use saved public history and are billed separately; they are not exact request replays or
          full correction cycles.
        

        

      

      

        
Method and practical limits

        

          Four independent workspaces use one frozen base, the same task for each model, thinking
          enabled, a nominal 32K context budget, 8K maximum output per request and capacity one.
          Three review instruction documents are configuration data; there are no model-specific
          runtime roles or score gates. Review rounds have no configured limit. A separate
          diagnostic manager monitors the user's weekly quota and restores the RTX server when local
          runs stop.
        

        

          Qwen runs on the RTX through Ollama; Flash calls the official DeepSeek API directly with
          proxy variables removed. Separate machines may run concurrently. No engine tuning or new
          model loading is mixed into this matrix. Preparation and code-snapshot instrumentation are
          included in wall time and reported separately. Buro builds its request view using a
          character-based token estimate; Ollama also receives num_ctx=32768, while the managed
          Flash service has its own larger native limit. Actual usage is reported rather than
          assumed from that estimate.
        

        

          Bars show observed model-request intervals, not GPU utilization. Buro orchestration is
          application control flow, not an invented orchestrator model. Code snapshots follow
          write/edit/delete/command completions; concurrent actions can share a snapshot, so
          attribution is observational. Reading a file is not a code change. Checkpoints use a
          private Git index and do not stage the agent's work.
        

        

          Review reports are model claims. A completed run or empty findings list does not prove
          correctness; host lint/types/tests/build and independent behavior checks are recorded
          separately. Nested-sandbox infrastructure failures remain visible. No privileges are
          weakened to make them pass. These are single task samples, not a statistically reliable
          leaderboard.
        

        

          Flash charges are calculated from actual streamed usage and cache counts using the
          official off-peak rates
          checked November 25, 2026: cached input $0.003, uncached input $0.15, output $0.60 per
          million tokens. Reasoning is already included in output. Wallet rounding/settlement can
          differ; no absolute balances are published. Qwen's API bill is zero, while power and
          hardware costs are not metered.
